A New Frontier in Wikitravel Data Representation

Some of our data representations will be unique to Wikitravel. No other organization will have them. The bigger shift, though, is the Turtle RDF standard.

Turtle lets us write custom RDF schemas directly. So we can build our own schemas with the same wiki techniques we already use. No separate platform needed.

You can even build a schema on our shared Wikitravel site, at Shared:Wikitravel:Schema. Once it exists, its elements become accessible in Turtle under the namespace wts: (Wikitravel schema).

That's where structured, scalable wiki data is going. #Wikitravel #RDF #DataScience #Technology

Now the head. Its dorsum is strongly longitudinally rugose, with 5–7 rugae between the frontal carinae at eye-level. These rugae are irregular and meander slightly, and a few anastomoses are usually present. The scrobal area is mostly smooth, but expect 1–2 fine rugulae crossing its width just behind the antennal fossa. Behind the eyes, the sides of the head are finely reticulate-rugose, and that sculpture runs around the posterior margins of the scrobe to the occiput. Between the rugae, the spaces are unsculptured, or at most show faint superficial traces.

The dorsal alitrunk is finely but strongly reticulate-rugose throughout, with broad, shining interspaces. The petiole dorsum is rugulose; the postpetiole ranges from rugulose to only faintly sculptured. The gaster is unsculptured. Every dorsal surface of head and body is densely clothed with fine, acute hairs. Color runs from dark reddish brown to blackish brown.

UPO-11: PprhJ Promoter Synthesis

Subject: foxl2 Expression Patterns in Trout: Key Findings

Dear Customer,

Here's what we found about foxl2 transcript expression in your study.

Both transcripts switch on very early in development (Figure 2). foxl2a showed highly restricted expression in the male. Its diverged paralog, foxl2b, turned up in most adult extragonadal tissues we examined (see Additional file 2).

In adult females, foxl2b sat almost entirely in three tissues: skin, gill, and ovary. In the testis, its expression was very strong. That matches earlier work showing foxl2b present while foxl2a is absent in later stages of testis development in trout [23].

Put together, these results point to foxl2b as a possible critical regulator of male-specific genes (such as cyp19b1), particularly later in development.

Thank you for your interest in our research.

Best regards,

[Your Name]

However, Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) cannot support carbon neutrality claims for electrical use beyond a claimant's metered consumption, since most RECs come from projects that were financially viable without their sale. [10] Consequently, they lack the essential attribute of additionality. Additionality asks a counterfactual question: what would have happened under the status quo had the REC not been purchased or contracted. Many additionality testing frameworks exist, but the core question stays the same: did the project's financial survival depend on REC revenues? Without verified proof of additionality, RECs cannot be treated as genuine emissions offsets.

We derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation, following the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975). From it, we obtained the higher-order dispersion relation for waves over an uneven bottom.

Then, using only the linear dispersion for steady waves, we recovered equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). The leading-order solution shows what matters: the modified curvature terms of the MMSE have significant effects, while the slope square terms stay negligible, as the mild-slope assumption requires. So we kept every modified curvature term the MSE drops. That gave us a uniform model.

To test it, we built a numerical model with the finite element method (FEM) that predicts wave scattering over a varying bottom. Across different sea beds, sinusoidal beds and man-made bars, the uniform model captures the main features of the waves. On sinusoidal beds, it matches the experimental data more closely than other established models. On man-made bars, both the MMSE and the uniform model match the data more closely than the results of Kirby (1986).

The FEM model also handles something harder: the transformation of waves over arbitrarily-varying bathymetry.

The myth of the Phaedrus is more intense than any earlier account, though it belongs to a different order. It concerns a former existence rather than a future one, and describes a struggle between reason, supported by passion or righteous indignation, and the animal instincts within us. In this life, the human soul has traveled in the company of some god and perceived truth in the form of the universal before birth, and our present existence is the result of a struggle that took place before. This world is a relative construct, often projected into a future, much as we wonder where men were before their birth or what awaits them after death. The question "Where were men before birth?" feels unfamiliar and unnatural to us, yet it is as influential and widespread as the other. In the Phaedrus, the "spiritual combat" of this life is only a figure of speech. The majesty and power of the whole passage, especially the proem beginning "The mind through all her being is immortal," can only be rendered inadequately in another language.

Here's something worth knowing about early hearing development. Children pick up spoken language in their first few years of life. A hearing impairment affects both sides of that: speaking and understanding what others say.

The trouble is that a severely hearing-impaired (deaf) child's deficit often goes unnoticed until communication problems have already strained the family and slowed the child's social skills. It doesn't have to go that way. A child raised in a Deaf community that uses sign language instead of speech avoids these problems entirely (please see our article on Deaf Culture).

That's why many developed countries screen newborns for hearing, so a deaf child isn't unknowingly isolated in a hearing family. Sign language is a complete way to communicate, but literacy still rests on understanding speech. In most written languages, word sounds are coded in symbols.

Consider the difference. Someone who heard well enough to learn speech and reading keeps that reading ability even after hearing deteriorates to the point where voices are gone. Someone who never heard well enough to learn to speak rarely reads well (see [4]). Most evidence points to one conclusion: identify hearing impairment early, and a child with very insensitive hearing has a real chance of learning spoken language. Listening also matters when learning a second language.

Transduction is how your body turns physical and chemical signals into neural impulses. In the nervous system, it is the basic process of translating stimuli into electrical signals. In sensory transduction, specialized sensory receptors take physical or chemical inputs and convert them into electrical impulses that travel to the brain.

Look at the visual system. In your retina, rod and cone cells form the bridge between the physical environment and neural communication. Light strikes these photoreceptors and changes the shape of the protein rhodopsin. That shift starts a cascade of events that alters the electrochemical gradient of the photoreceptor. As the gradient drops, so do the electrical signals sent to the brain. More light hitting the photoreceptor means fewer electrical impulses. That inversion is how your brain decodes the visual world with such precision.

Mobile Gaming: The Next Evolution of Co-Creation

Mobile internet is changing what storytelling can do. Games now run on portable, location-aware interfaces, and that opens a door no earlier interactive media could open. For decades, electronic games have tried to make the player a co-author alongside the original designers instead of just an avatar in a gameworld. Mobile games get us closer than ever.

Here's what these interfaces allow: you can pull places from the physical world into your gameworld, and push the gameworld back out into real places. Beyond that, mobile games drop linear narratives. The story gets built cooperatively, and it depends on your experience of place.

The "author-player" idea isn't new. But mobile games push it past the limits of the traditional video game. They extend worldmaking beyond the screen, into the physical world, and they turn what you see, hear, and feel in real places into storytelling tools.

In our essay, we theorize the storytelling potential unique to mobile games, then describe what happened when we tried to use it ourselves: designing and implementing our hybrid-reality game, University of Death.

Subject: Tips for Hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area, Germany

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), or just the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It grew out of former industrial cities: Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, and Witten.

Roughly five million people live here. That is far more than Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. The motorway density is high, yet hitchhiking can still be hard, because the minor roads form a complicated network. The main motorways are the A1, A2, and A3.

So if you plan to hitch here, stick to those primary motorways. Avoid the smaller roads; hardly any transit traffic uses them, which makes them very hard to work with. Germany is generally a pleasant country for hitchhiking, but the Ruhr Area is by far its most unpleasant part in this respect. Hitching inside the Ruhr Area is like hitching in a big city such as Istanbul. Each city is independent, yet to a traveler they all feel like districts of one huge city.

We hope this helps you plan a safe and enjoyable trip.

Best regards,

Subject: Study Results: Lung Tissue Volume and Aeration Analysis

Dear Customer,

Here are the results you asked for on lung tissue volume and functional changes.

We calculated total lung tissue volume as: volume of lung tissue = number of voxels × volume of the voxel. This holds whenever the compartment considered has a CT number above zero.

For ΔFRC, the change in functional residual capacity from PEEP withdrawal, we took the difference in total gas volume in the whole lung between PEEP and ZEEP states. Alveolar derecruitment was the difference in gas volume within poorly aerated and nonaerated regions between those same two states.

We also measured gas volume lost to PEEP withdrawal in the normally aerated regions, defined by CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).

Then, per reference [21], we classified each patient's lung morphology, the distribution of lost aeration, as diffuse, patchy, or lobar, based on CT attenuations at ZEEP.
